title: Wreck and Horizon
premise: Felix Reyes, a railroad engineer who maps closed lines and never stays anywhere long enough to be missed, salvages a river-locked chest stamped with the seal of Vaskaria, a nation erased from every map she trusts. Inside are survey documents proving a forbidden source upstream — and proof that her late mentor helped bury it. Hunted by a salvage syndicate and shadowed by a Vaskarian exile who wants the truth restored, Felix must pilot a derelict work train up the dead line to the river's headwaters before the dry season strands them all. At the source, she must choose between selling the secret that would finally buy her a safe, settled life and publishing it, which costs her everything except the found family she stopped running from. She publishes it.
about_author: Jude Lockridge is a former track inspector who spent a decade riding freight lines across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who fix things in places that want to stay broken.

chapters.title: The Last Open Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Working a decaying branch line, Felix surveys a bridge scheduled for demolition and quietly records it on her map of closed lines before moving on. The beat is restless competence: she is excellent at leaving, and we feel the cost of it in what she doesn't say goodbye to.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. After a storm floods the rail yard, Felix wades in to free a jammed culvert and finds a chest wedged in the debris, stamped with an unfamiliar double-eagle seal. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution — for once, she stops moving.

chapters.title: A Nation With No Address
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In a riverside archive she learns the seal belongs to Vaskaria, a country dissolved forty years ago and scrubbed from atlases. The chest holds survey charts pointing upstream to a 'forbidden source.' Beat: vertigo — the map she trusted has holes shaped like people.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Trains
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Dain Kovic, a Vaskarian exile tracking rumors of the chest for his scattered community. He locates Felix but hesitates to reveal himself. Beat: longing — a man who has spent his life looking backward sees a chance to look forward.

chapters.title: Buyers at the Yard
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A salvage syndicate called the Meridian Combine makes Felix a generous offer for the chest, then a threat when she stalls. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance; she recognizes their kind — they buy things and erase the people attached to them.

chapters.title: Dain
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. He finally approaches Felix at a night market, proves his knowledge of the chest's contents, and asks not for it but for passage upstream. Beat: wary negotiation between two people who both survive by trusting no one.

chapters.title: Mentor's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Among the charts Felix finds annotations in the handwriting of Oren Vasquez, the mentor who taught her engineering and taught her to run. He helped seal the source. Beat: betrayal — the one person she belonged to was part of the erasure.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Felix calculates water levels: the upper river will become impassable in six weeks. The Combine buys the rail corridor out from under her. Beat: the trap closing — staying means fighting, and fighting means roots.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. To move a derelict work train, Felix recruits people nobody else would hire: a disgraced dispatcher named Ilsa, twin boilermakers, and a teenage stowaway, Pip. Beat: reluctant warmth — a crew assembling itself around her whether she consents or not.

chapters.title: First Water
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The train departs up the dead line through flooded cuttings. The Combine's first sabotage attempt nearly wrecks them at a trestle. Beat: trial by fire — the strays hold together, and Felix realizes she's no longer traveling alone.

chapters.title: Closed Stations
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The crew shelters in an abandoned station where Vaskarian refugees once lived; Pip finds children's chalk drawings still on a wall. Beat: grief made tangible — the erasure wasn't abstract, it had bedrooms.

chapters.title: Oren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Decoding Oren's annotations, Felix learns he sealed the source to protect refugees hiding in its valley, trading truth for safety. Beat: painful empathy — her mentor's lie was also a shelter, and she must decide if lies can be load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Combine Catches Up
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Meridian agents board the train disguised as inspectors; Dain exposes them but takes a knife wound doing it. Beat: loyalty proven in blood — the exile bleeds for a crew that isn't his, and becomes theirs.

chapters.title: High Desert, Low Water
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The river shallows; the train labors through a canyon as the dry season accelerates. Rations tighten, tempers fray, and Pip runs off after a fight. Beat: pressure — found family tested by scarcity, not just danger.

chapters.title: Stowaway Found
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix tracks Pip to a cliff shrine left by Vaskarian herders and brings him back, admitting aloud that she's afraid too. Beat: vulnerability — the woman who never stops moving admits why: everyone she stayed for left first.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Combine's director intercepts them by radio with a final offer: sell the charts, receive money enough to retire anywhere, forever. Beat: temptation laid bare — everything Felix ever wanted, priced against everyone she now loves.

chapters.title: Night Vote
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Around the caboose stove, each crew member says what the source means to them, and Felix puts the choice to a vote instead of deciding alone. Beat: belonging — for the first time, she builds a decision with people instead of fleeing ahead of one.

chapters.title: The Last Gradient
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The final climb exceeds anything the locomotive can do; the crew lightens the engine, hand-spikes the wheels, and pushes it up the last grade on foot through the night. Beat: collective triumph — impossible made possible only together.

chapters.title: Source
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. They reach the headwaters: a spring-fed valley where descendants of hidden Vaskarians still live, unregistered and unseen for two generations. Beat: awe and ache — the forbidden place is full of ordinary people keeping an extraordinary secret alive.

chapters.title: Meridian at the Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Combine arrives by helicopter with contracts and guns; the director offers Felix the deal one last time as the valley watches. Beat: climax of character — Felix tears up the contract on camera and names the valley and its people to the world.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Journalists, cartographers, and Vaskarian exiles flood in; the map is redrawn publicly, with Oren Vasquez's role told honestly, shelter and betrayal alike. Beat: bittersweet reckoning — truth restores more than it destroys, but not without cost.

chapters.title: Wreck and Horizon
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Months later, Felix opens a new rail office in the valley town, her map of closed lines reframed on the wall beside a chart of open ones. Pip apprentices under her; Dain plants a garden. Beat: resolution — the woman who kept moving finally built something worth staying for.
